relations.relation: identify discrete abstraction, indirection, or metaprogramming units present in the candidate solution
determine whether each identified construct is invoked by a stated requirement or concrete call site
detect dynamic, reflective, or hidden-default behavior versus explicit direct code paths for each construct
compare identified constructs against their necessity signals to flag speculative or unused abstraction
compare count and defaultedness of configuration options against a minimal explicit configuration set
locates each layer of abstraction, indirection, or metaprogramming construct introduced beyond a direct solution
links each located construct to a concrete, currently-active requirement it serves
compares the construct's complexity against a minimal alternative that satisfies the same currently-active requirement
enumerates configuration knobs/settings and whether their purpose is explicit versus implicit
flags generality, hooks, or extension points not exercised by any present call site
delimits the code span or module boundary over which simplicity/explicitness is assessed
locates uses of reflection, dynamic dispatch, decorators, or code generation that introduce implicit behavior
enumerates exposed parameters, flags, and defaults introduced by the unit
compares each abstraction layer against its current call sites to flag generality not required by any existing caller
contrasts the candidate against a hypothetical minimal-explicit rewrite to size the complexity gap attributable to the unit

metric.name: Simplicity, explicitness, and avoidance of over‑engineering
metric.text: Favor simple, explicit solutions; hide unnecessary magic/metaprogramming; keep configuration minimal and explicit; avoid speculative abstractions.
